cim: Senators Will Weigh Caregiver Artificial Intelligence Risks
cim_eredeti: Senators Will Weigh Caregiver Artificial Intelligence Risks
szoveg_eredeti:
Artificial intelligence (AI) tools for caregivers, their opportunities and their threats, are the subject of a Senate hearing. The Senate Special Committee on Aging will hold an AI caregiving hearing on Dec. 2, titled "Hearings to Examine Caregivers and AI, Focusing on Opportunities, Challenges, and Threats." ​

Sen. Rick Scott (R-FL) chairs the committee, and Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) is the ranking member. The title frames the session around opportunities, challenges and threats, so testimony could cover both the promise of caregiving tools and their risks.

On Nov. 18, the Department of Health and Human Services announced 19 first-phase winners of its Caregiver AI Prize Challenge, who will share $2.25 million.

An AARP report published Nov. 19 found caregivers age 50 and older most interested in AI for understanding health information, while 89% said they were cautious about using AI-powered caregiving tools.

Lobbying disclosures show clients active on both halves of the topic. AARP Inc. reported $40,000 with Thorn Run Partners for each of the first three quarters of 2026, including the third quarter, on expanding support for caregivers, including federal paid leave. Among AI clients:

Lobbyists and staff should watch whether testimony engages the federal prize program or the paid-leave and caregiver-support issues AARP lobbies on. The committee will meet on Dec. 2.
